## 2. The weighted-residence theorem

Consider a canonically identified family of finite minus lobes with:

- at most \(\ell=O(1)\) neck bonds;
- total affected principal perimeter between a sufficiently large logarithmic threshold and \(P_0=K_0R\);
- all affected island boundaries included in that perimeter;
- all thermal interiors retained through their actual conditional Gibbs laws.

For this family, the construction produces a physical current \(F\) satisfying
\[
\operatorname{div}F=w1_E-q+\rho,
\]
with
\[
0\le q\le b_-w,\qquad
|\rho|\le\xi w,\qquad
\left|\frac{F(e)}{g(e)}\right|\le\mathsf H.
\]

Here \(b_-\) is an explicit contour-word tail, and
\[
\mathsf H
\le
\operatorname{poly}_\theta(n,r,P_0)\,
K^{P_0}n^{P_0/(2r)}
e^{Cm_\theta P_0+C_\theta\ell},
\]
where
\[
m_\theta=\frac23\sum_{P\ge4}P(3e^{-3\theta/2})^P.
\]

Because the actual soft potential \(v\) is decreasing, its physical current is upward and has total edge current at most
\[
k_*C_\kappa,\qquad k_*=\lceil n/2\rceil.
\]
Summation by parts therefore gives
\[
\boxed{
N_E:=\sum_Ewv
\le
(b_-+\xi)N_\kappa+\mathsf H k_*C_\kappa.
}
\tag{1}
\]

This is a bound on the actual weighted residence. The terminal image \(q\) is accounted for explicitly; it is not silently treated as having reached the target.

### How the current is constructed

The construction fills the net minus lobe in row-major order while preserving plus islands. Except at the bounded neck, each flip has two plus neighbors, so the bare barrier is \(O(J\ell)\), independent of lobe diameter.

The thermal part uses a common guarded contour catalogue. For effective fields \(|b_i|\le\phi\), its partition function satisfies
\[
\partial_{b_i}\log F(b)
=\mathbb E_b\tau_i
\ge1-2m_\theta>0.
\]
Thus replacing a minus base site by a plus base site increases the common thermal factor. Only the initial guard loss and neck barrier are paid.

Each base flip is lifted through **actual physical thermal redistribution**, a guarded physical flip, and redistribution into the next fiber. Intermediate full marginals telescope. A source decoder records boundary words, roots, the filling stage, and remnant information. Small affected fragments remain marked until they disappear.

The resulting expected current has a finite constructive description and an explicit bound. Its exponentially large edge table need not be formed.
